quotes.quote: We introduce PerceptionBench, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the atomic visual perception capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
Since PerceptionBench targets visual perception, we retain only the perception error class, whose ten error types we adopt as the ten atomic perceptual capabilities evaluated by PerceptionBench
Any image whose similarity exceeds a strict threshold of 0.95, i.e., near-duplicate or leaked images, is discarded.
we therefore evaluate all candidate samples with an ensemble of four frontier MLLMs
The decomposition and annotation are performed by more than ten professional annotators with extensive experience in multimodal evaluation.
Samples requiring external knowledge, unsupported assumptions, or information beyond the visual input are removed to prevent evaluation from being dominated by non-perceptual factors.
As shown in Figure 5, PerceptionBench contains 3,000 verified samples spanning the ten atomic perceptual capabilities identified from the failure-driven capability discovery process.

In terms of construction source, 1,800 of the 3,000 questions (60%) are atomic sub-questions decomposed from attributed failures on the source benchmarks, while the remaining 1,200 (40%) are newly authored on supplemented images
the remaining error classes of the induced taxonomy are used exclusively for failure attribution during construction
all models are evaluated with unified prompts and official inference settings where available
For each model, we adopt the highest available reasoning budget.
In total, 1.1% of its reported answers are produced by Claude-Opus-4.8.
We therefore employ GPT-oss-120B as a unified judge model that compares each model response against the reference answer for automatic evaluation
On a random sample of 300 predictions, the automatic evaluation agrees with human judgments on 299 cases (99.7%)
Overall accuracy spans 32.5% (GLM-4.6V) to 59.7%, so the benchmark retains strong discriminative power far from any ceiling effect.
Across models, perception-related hallucination has the lowest average accuracy (36.7%), well below visual relation (53.2%), OCR (52.4%), and localization (52.0%).
GPT-5.6-Sol, the overall leader, reaches 76.7% on localization but only 26.9% on hallucination, one of the lowest hallucination scores in the leaderboard.
yet even the strongest models leave every capability below 80%.
Kimi K3 trails the overall leader by only 1.2 points.
the full benchmark is slightly harder than the released subset for most capabilities

In addition, we report pass@4 (the proportion of samples solved in at least one of the four runs) and pass4 (the proportion of samples solved in all four runs), which characterize the capability upper bound and the behavioral consistency of each model, respectively.
although the aggregate score is stable, per-sample perceptual behavior is not
The benchmark evaluates MLLMs across ten atomic perceptual capabilities identified from failure-driven capability induction.
Each model is evaluated with four independent runs.
Asserts objects, text, or values that do not exist in the image.
Our taxonomy is induced from the failures of the current model generation, so it reflects today’s weaknesses rather than a fixed structure of perception.
Failure attribution also relies on a stronger analyzer model, and residual attribution errors may propagate into capability labels.
Finally, PerceptionBench isolates perception by design, so capability scores do not directly predict end-to-end task performance; the benchmark is best used alongside task-oriented suites.
Our own annotations and newly authored questions are released under Apache-2.0.
source-derived samples remain subject to the licenses of their origin benchmarks
The reference answer is absolutely correct; judge solely by whether the student’s final result matches it, even if the solution process is correct.
a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities
Across sixteen frontier MLLMs, no model reaches 60% accuracy, and perception-related hallucination is the weakest capability on average.
The retained and constructed samples together form an in-house pool of 17,000+ verified questions.
Perception, Not Reasoning or Knowledge: Samples are curated, decomposed, and difficulty-balanced so that difficulty stems from perception rather than reasoning or external knowledge.
Each source benchmark captures a narrow slice of perception errors, and these slices overlap only weakly (mean pairwise weighted Jaccard 0.20).

is a benchmark that focuses on atomic visual perception capabilities.
By construction source, 1,800 (60%) are atomic sub-questions decomposed from attributed failures on the source benchmarks, while the remaining 1,200 (40%) are newly authored on supplemented images.
The 3,000 questions are subsampled with capability-level balancing and difficulty stratification from the constructed portion of an in-house pool of 17,000+ verified samples
Sixteen frontier MLLMs (ten proprietary, six open-source) are evaluated with unified prompts and the highest available reasoning budget.
GPT-oss-120B judges each response against the reference (agreement with human judgment: 99.7% on a 300-sample audit).
The evaluator feeds question + images to the model, then asks the judge to grade the free-form answer against the reference with the paper's teacher-grading prompt
Per-item predictions are written to results/PerceptionBench_<model>.jsonl and overall/per-category accuracy to results/PerceptionBench_<model>_scores.json
